In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 5' UTR of a gene can be a major determinant of translation initiation, elongation, and termination.
the 3′ UTR is the most important part of the mRNA for regulating the stability of the mRNA and therefore the translation of the mRNA.
a 50-nucleotide coding gap is not detrimental to translation, but it is less efficiently bypassed by polysomes than by monosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coding gap is not an absolute block to translation, and the presence of the gap can be tolerated by the cell, but the presence of a coding gap does have a negative impact on translation.

the presence of a coding gap in a transcript can be detrimental for the expression of the gene, but the extent to which it affects expression depends on the transcript structure, the presence of a 3' UTR and the type of cell.
we have identified an important mechanism for the control of translation initiation and ribosome loading on mRNAs in eukaryotes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an important role for mRNA structure in regulating the efficiency of translation elongation.
, in addition to their role in translation, mRNA structures can affect mRNA stability.
the 3′ UTR is not just a passive element of the mRNA, but an active player in translation regulation.
